# dtcloud_lb (Data Source)

Looks up one load balancer by ID.

Lookup is by id rather than by name, because load balancer names are not unique.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Lookup is by id: load balancer names are not unique.
data "dtcloud_lb" "existing" {
  id = "3d372446-4c75-4327-9511-98442456162f"
}

# The VIP sits on a network block rather than a top-level field.
output "vip" {
  value = data.dtcloud_lb.existing.network[0].ip
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) ID of the load balancer.

### Read-Only

- `balancing_pools` (Number) Number of balancing pools.
- `created_on` (String) Creation timestamp as reported by the API.
- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `flavor_name` (String) Human-readable flavor name.
- `floating_ip` (String) Floating IP, when one is associated.
- `high_availability` (String) High-availability mode.
- `members_state` (List of String) Operating state of each member.
- `members_total` (Number) Total number of members.
- `name` (String) Name of the load balancer.
- `network` (List of Object) The network the load balancer's VIP sits on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--network))
- `status` (String) Provisioning status.

<a id="nestedatt--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `ip` (String)
- `name` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Use this for a load balancer Terraform did not create.** Declaring it as a resource instead would
  hand Terraform ownership, and a later destroy would take down everything behind it.
* **The VIP is reported inside `network`**, not as a top-level field.
* **`status` is one title-case word.** `Disabled` means no listener yet, `Unknown` means a pool with
  no health monitor; neither is a failure.
